item.title: The Four Periodic Inscription Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.24376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that four periodic curves in $\mathbb{C}$ inscribe a family of isosceles trapezoids for every angle $\theta\in(0,\pi)$, whose similarity types are determined by the signed areas between the quotients of the curves in the infinite cylinder. In the smooth case, the problem is identified with a Lagrangian intersection problem in $\mathbb{R}\times S^1\times\mathbb{C}$, while the continuous case follows by a convergence argument.
item.dc:creator: Ali Naseri Sadr

item.title: Contractible Closed Reeb Orbits on Prequantization Bundles under Weak Index Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.24557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the multiplicity of contractible closed Reeb orbits on prequantization circle bundles. Building on the existing multiplicity result Theorem 1.3 for closed Reeb orbits on prequantization $S^1$-bundles, we weaken the index assumptions by requiring only that the supporting contact form has no contractible periodic Reeb orbits with mean Conley-Zehnder index zero and no contractible good periodic Reeb orbits with Conley-Zehnder index 0, and we obtain a lower bound for the number of geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits carried by contact forms $\alpha$ on a prequantization $S^1$-bundle under certain natural topological assumptions (Theorem 1.6). In dimension five we further relax the index assumptions and show that, under a mild index condition imposed only on simple contractible periodic orbits and the same topological assumptions on the prequantization $S^1$-bundle, every non-degenerate supporting contact form carries at least $\dim H_*(B;\mathbb{Q})$ geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits (Theorem 1.11), in agreement with the conjectural lower bound for prequantization bundles.
item.dc:creator: Peng Liu, Dong Xie

item.title: Symplectophagy
item.description: arXiv:2610.24862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of a symplectophagy, which is a symplectic isotopy satisfying conditions reminiscent of the symplectic camel. We present new symplectic rigidity results which take the form of obstructions to the existence of symplectophagies in certain situations. The main tool is the relative symplectic cohomology recently introduced by Varolgunes, as well as its extension to pairs, due to the authors and L. Polterovich, for which we establish an invariance property, which is the chief technical novelty of the present paper. An important role is also played by the recent calculations of relative symplectic cohomology in complex projective spaces due to Dickstein-Ganor.
item.dc:creator: Adi Dickstein, Yaniv Ganor, Frol Zapolsky

item.title: Equivariant Moment Maps and the Ricci Cocycle in Weighted Fujiki--Donaldson Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.24543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$,. We discuss weighted Fujiki--Donaldson theory with respect to the measure $d\nu=e^h\omega^n/n! $ for an arbitrary smooth real-valued function $h$ on $M$. We prove that the group generated by the flows of Hamiltonians that Poisson-commute with $h$ always admits an equivariant moment map for its action on the full space of $\omega$-compatible almost complex structures. The moment map takes values in the continuous dual of the Lie algebra. Its density is expressed in terms of the Hermitian scalar curvature, a local weight correction, and an $L^\infty$ function $r_h^0$ constructed from the long-time average of the polar determinant phase. The function $r_h^0$ can be regarded as a Ruelle-type asymptotic density incorporating phase comparison via a connection. The key step in the proof is to represent the Ricci cocycle as the coboundary of a continuous cochain constructed from $r_h^0$. We also consider the action of the exact volume-preserving diffeomorphism group on a connected component of the space of almost complex structures inducing the given orientation on a closed connected oriented manifold of real dimension $2n$. In contrast to the weighted Hamiltonian setting, we prove that, for $n>1$, this action admits an equivariant moment map if and only if the real first Chern class vanishes.
item.dc:creator: Ryushi Goto

item.title: K\"ahler-Ricci Flow is Symplectic Deflation plus an Exact Symplectic Deformation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24825v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate that K\"ahler-Ricci flow on a Fano surface decomposes as a symplectic deflation along a plurianticanonical divisor plus an exact symplectic deformation in the divisor complement. We apply this decomposition to the study of certain projective bundles. We establish the optimal decay rate in the setting of Song, Sz\'ekelyhidi, and Weinkove for a family of toric metrics which match the cohomological profile of K\"ahler-Ricci flow. In doing so, we identify a $C^2$-obstruction to proving the optimal decay rate in the setting of ruled toric surfaces. We present these ideas as a new symplectic-topological approach to the study of K\"ahler-Ricci flow.
item.dc:creator: Randall R. Van Why

item.title: Stein fillable contact structures with half Giroux torsion
item.description: arXiv:2610.24922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that there exist Stein fillable contact 3-manifolds which contain a separating half Giroux torsion layer. Our examples are on Seifert fibred spaces over the sphere.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Cavallo, Irena Matkovi\v{c}

item.title: Weighted homogeneous surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings
item.description: arXiv:2610.24936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study rational homology disk smoothings through canonical-cover representations and specialization of reflexive canonical powers, and recover the known dual graph and analytic classification. The geometric-genus representation of the canonical covering group, together with its complex conjugate, is a direct summand of the reduced regular representation. Specialization forces the canonical Riemann--Roch corrections to vanish; explicit formulas give equations for the Seifert invariants. For three arms and central weight two, these equations, the character restrictions, and the numerical identities determine the Seifert data without assuming the existence of a smoothing. Projective compactifications treat the remaining cases, and elliptic pencils explain the four-arm attachment points and the parameter independence of their cross ratios. We construct strong $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein smoothings for all listed analytic structures by deforming canonical-cover equations and lifting generators of the full first syzygy module. The numerical Milnor formula gives rational homology disk fibers.
item.dc:creator: Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin

item.title: Integrable building blocks for symplectic neural networks: learned-type layers, fiber-preserving layers, and what a single layer can do
item.description: arXiv:2610.25023v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Exactly symplectic neural networks are built almost exclusively from shear maps and gain expressivity only through depth. We ask what else a single explicit symplectic layer can be. Observing that every layer in use is the exact flow of a Hamiltonian that is a function of commuting integrals, we obtain three families of layers: a learned-type layer, in which every conjugate pair is rotated, squeezed or sheared by a state-dependent amount and the type is found by training; moving-plane shears, residual symplectic maps outside the known ridge-function class; and fiber-preserving layers, which combine an unconstrained point transformation with a fiber translation at the cost of one linear solve. We characterize residual symplectic layers $x \mapsto x + J\nabla H(x)$: in one degree of freedom they are exactly the shears along a line, while from two degrees of freedom on a strictly larger class exists. Conjugating a learned-type layer by a symplectic network yields an exact one-parameter group with an exactly conserved learned Hamiltonian. In experiments on sixteen systems with one to forty degrees of freedom, against SympNets, H\'enonNets and learned-plane shear networks, layers built on nonlinear integrals are far more accurate when the Hamiltonian contains functions of those integrals. On nonlinear Schr\"odinger lattices with six to forty sites, twist layers alternating with linear symplectic maps are over a hundred times more accurate than every shear-based network, and with an on-site potential of learned form three to four orders of magnitude more accurate. On chains of Tao oscillators with the step size as an input, stretch layers are 45 to 70 times more accurate than learned-plane shears and recover the Hamiltonian to 1%. On generic non-separable systems, fiber layers improve on learned-plane shears by at most a factor of two, and widening the networks does not help any architecture.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Qing He

item.title: Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.25042v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.
item.dc:creator: Cengiz Aydin, Chankyu Joung

item.title: The classification of taut surface singularities via representations from logarithmic vector fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.25654v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study logarithmic vector fields on exceptional cycles through finite-dimensional representations and recover Laufer's classification of taut normal complex surface singularities. For graphs with two nodes, restriction maps define representations of a fixed quiver, with dimensions bounded independently of the number of components and their self-intersections. We identify restriction cohomology with an extension group and use interval decomposition to reduce its vanishing to interpolation on a rational chain. These calculations determine the classification conditions, and vanishing on every analytic realization proves sufficiency, including the nonrational cases. The obstruction cycles also give a uniform criterion: a graph is taut if and only if $H^1(5E,S_X|_{5E})=0$ for every analytic realization, where $S_X$ is the ambient logarithmic tangent bundle. We prove that five is the smallest positive integer for which this criterion holds for all graphs.
item.dc:creator: Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin

item.title: Non-planar contact structures with Calabi-Yau Fillings and topological quantum computation
item.description: arXiv:2610.25878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is a non-planar counterpart of the author's earlier work on planar contact structures and topological quantum computation. There the page is planar and all branch points are paired by disjoint liftable arcs, compatibly with the joint eigenlines of the Ising representation and with Calabi-Yau (CY) Stein fillings, those with vanishing first Chern class. Here the page has genus g and connected binding, presented as a simple degree-three cover of the disk. Every maximal system of disjoint liftable arcs has exactly g members and leaves two branch points unused. The half-twist interchanging the two points is not liftable, but its cube is, and lifts to the identity. An integral residue criterion supplies the CY test. A factorization localized on a contact connected sum is automatically CY. Unlike in the planar case, a CY factorization need not be the shortest. Once the fusion channels of the g pairs are fixed, Ising fusion determines the channel of the remaining pair, and braiding acts there only by scalars. Fibonacci fusion can leave that channel undetermined, and the powers of the cube then act by ten distinct relative phases on a single joint eigenspace, while the CY Stein filling stays fixed
item.dc:creator: Atsuhide Mori

item.title: A new look at unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction for toric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2412.17157v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a symplectic manifold $M$ with the Hamiltonian action of a compact Lie group $G$, we give a new perspective on the problem of unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence. We argue that this correspondence leads naturally to the introduction of what we call Fourier polarizations, whose real directions include the Hamiltonian vector fields of all invariant functions of the moment map. For a Fourier polarization, quantization commutes with reduction unitarily. For a general $G$-invariant polarization, $\mathcal{P}$, unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence can then be formulated in terms of the existence of a Fourier polarization, $\mathcal{P}_F$, such that the quantizations with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ and to $\mathcal{P}_F$ are unitarily equivalent. We describe this perspective in detail for symplectic toric manifolds, by considering symplectic reductions associated to the action of a subtorus $T^p\subset T^n$. We consider half-form quantization in Fourier (mixed) polarizations $\mathcal{P}_\infty$, whose real directions are generated by(the Hamiltonian vector fields of the)components of the $T^p$ moment map. We show that Fourier mixed polarizations of this type can be obtained by Mabuchi geodesic rays of toric K\"ahler structures, starting at a given initial structure and with velocity given by the norm square of the moment map of the torus subgroup. We lift these geodesic rays to the quantum bundle via generalized coherent state transforms, which define equivariant isomorphisms between quantum Hilbert spaces for the K\"ahler and Fourier polarizations, where the later are obtained at infinite geodesic time. Unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction in these cases then becomes equivalent to the unitarity of these isomorphisms. In general, however, in the toric case, these isomorphisms are not unitary.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e M. Mour\~ao, Jo\~ao P. Nunes, Augusto Pereira, Dan Wang

item.title: Periodic Inscription of Isosceles Trapezoids
item.description: arXiv:2503.04077v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a pair of continuous disjoint periodic curves in $\mathbb{C}$ inscribes an isosceles trapezoid with any similarity type. The case of smooth curves can be identified with a Lagrangian intersection problem for a pair of Lagrangian cylinders in $\mathbb{R}\times S^1\times\mathbb{C}$, and the continuous case follows from the smooth one by a standard convergence argument.
item.dc:creator: Ali Naseri Sadr

item.title: Reeb orbits frequently intersecting a symplectic surface
item.description: arXiv:2504.19332v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider a symplectic surface in a three-dimensional contact manifold with boundary on Reeb orbits (periodic orbits of the Reeb vector field). We assume that the rotation numbers of the boundary Reeb orbits satisfy a certain inequality, and we also make a technical assumption that the Reeb vector field has a particular ``nice'' form near the boundary of the surface. We then show that there exist Reeb orbits which intersect the interior of the surface, with a lower bound on the frequency of these intersections in terms of the symplectic area of the surface and the contact volume of the three-manifold. No genericity of the contact form is assumed. As a corollary of the main result, we obtain a generalization of various recent results relating the mean action of periodic orbits to the Calabi invariant for area-preserving surface diffeomorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hutchings

item.title: Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures
item.description: arXiv:2608.30031v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the geography of taut foliations on compact $3$-manifolds with toroidal boundary components. The central object of our work is the set of boundary multislopes realized by foliations transverse to a fixed flow on such a manifold. We prove that these sets exhibit remarkable structural properties (rationality, rigidity, and convexity) which motivate the name ziggurats. Our main tool, of independent interest, is a two-way correspondence between foliations and contact structures on $3$-manifolds with boundary: we generalize the Eliashberg-Thurston theorem, which produces pairs of positive and negative contact structures from foliations, and a construction of the first author, which builds foliations from such contact pairs. Using both directions of this correspondence, we bring contact-geometric methods to bear on the architecture of ziggurats.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Massoni, Jonathan Zung

item.title: Positivity of Wahl defects and specialization of reflexive powers of the canonical sheaf
item.description: arXiv:2610.21092v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(X,E) \to (V,0)$ be the minimal good resolution of a normal complex surface singularity, with $E$ reduced. The Wahl defect is $\Delta(V,0) :=h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2 S_X)$, where $S_X=\Theta_X(-\log E)$. For non-Gorenstein $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein singularities $(V,0)$, we prove that $\Delta(V,0)\geq0$, with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case. This proves Wahl's Main Conjecture in this class and his $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein and Rational Conjectures. The proof expresses $\Delta$ as the multiplicity of the canonical character in a representation constructed from differential forms and residues. We also prove $\Delta+4p_g\geq0$ for arbitrary normal surface singularities, with equality precisely for rational quasi-homogeneous singularities. For smoothings of rational surface singularities, we give a Riemann--Roch formula for the lengths of the cokernels of the restriction maps to the central fiber for all reflexive canonical powers, in terms of the Milnor number and periodic local Riemann--Roch corrections. This yields numerical and representation-theoretic criteria for $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein smoothings, defined as quotients of equivariant smoothings of the index-one cover with trivial group action on the base. If a rational singularity admits a $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein smoothing, such smoothings are precisely those with minimal Milnor number, or equivalently those whose smoothing components have minimal dimension. Combining these results, we prove that every rational homology disk smoothing is $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein, has a rational weighted homogeneous central fiber, and occurs over a one-dimensional smoothing component. Together with the known weighted homogeneous classification, this completes the analytic classification of normal surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings.
item.dc:creator: Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin

item.title: Nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth curves and arbitrarily negative Wahl defects
item.description: arXiv:2610.21093v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a theory of nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth projective curves of genus at least two, constructed by gluing products of open subsets of a curve with a disc using nonlinear changes of the disc coordinate. Their zero sections have normal bundles of negative degree and contract to normal surface singularities. For the minimal good resolution $(X,E) \to (V,0)$ of a normal complex surface singularity other than a rational double point, the Wahl defect is defined by $\Delta(V,0) := h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2S_X)$, where $E$ is reduced and $S_X = \Theta_X(-\log E)$. We give a finite formula for this defect in terms of extension obstructions when $E$ is a single smooth curve. For our constructed neighborhoods, the formula involves extensions of functions alone, includes obstructions at every order, and gives a sharp lower bound depending only on the genus. We apply the theory to hyperelliptic curves and smooth plane curves. Both families consist of singularities that are neither $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein nor quasi-homogeneous. The hyperelliptic examples realize every nonpositive integer as a Wahl defect and attain the genus bound in every genus at least two. They disprove Wahl's Main Conjecture, which asserts nonnegativity for non-Gorenstein singularities, with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case.
item.dc:creator: Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin
